name: DBMS & SQL
blurb: One best video per subtopic, drawn from Stanford's database course, CMU's database course and the best SQL teachers on YouTube, each with a deeper and a quicker alternative. Watch the best pick, then do that subtopic's MCQs.
method:
• Best pick: the clearest correct explanation at interview depth. For SQL and theory most come from Jennifer Widom's Stanford course (short, exact lectures); for design, joins and normalization from Decomplexify; for interview-style queries from techTFQ.
  • Go deeper: Andy Pavlo's CMU 15-445 lectures on how a database actually implements indexes, joins and concurrency control, and Martin Kleppmann (author of Designing Data-Intensive Applications) on distributed data.
  • Quick / visual: short refreshers for revision.
  • Candidates came from Hacker News comments that link YouTube plus YouTube search for every subtopic. High-view exam channels lost when an English lecture explained the same idea more precisely; FD closure and candidate-key numericals are covered by the linked MCQs.

subtopics.name: Full courses
subtopics.note: CMU 15-445 is the best database course online, but it teaches how to build a database. For interviews, use it for indexing and transactions and the picks below for everything else.

picks.title: CMU Intro to Database Systems (15-445/645 - Fall 2024)
picks.why: Andy Pavlo's course: storage, buffer pools, B+trees, hashing, join algorithms, query optimisation, two-phase locking, MVCC, recovery and distributed databases. The most-recommended database course on Hacker News (13 users linked its 2019 edition).

picks.title: Relational database (RDBMS)
picks.why: Keys, ER diagrams, joins and normal forms with clear examples: the design half of DBMS interviews.

picks.title: Database Engineering
picks.why: A backend engineer on how Postgres and MySQL behave in practice: indexes, isolation, locks, replication and sharding. Dip in by topic; don't watch it all.

subtopics.name: DBMS Fundamentals & Keys
subtopics.note: Super, candidate, primary, foreign and surrogate keys; ER modelling and cardinality; relational algebra (selection, projection, joins, division).

picks.title: Database Keys Made Easy - Primary, Foreign, Candidate, Surrogate, & Many More
picks.why: Every kind of key on one running example, with the reasoning for choosing a primary key, natural vs surrogate.

picks.title: Entity Relationship Diagrams
picks.why: Entities, relationships and cardinality, then turning the diagram into tables.

picks.title: 05-01-relational-algebra-1.mp4
picks.why: Jennifer Widom (Stanford) on select, project, product and join, with the exact semantics SQL is built on.

picks.title: #01 - Relational Model & Algebra (CMU Intro to Database Systems)
picks.why: Why the relational model won, and relational algebra as a database actually executes it.

subtopics.name: SQL Basics & NULL Handling
subtopics.note: SELECT/WHERE/ORDER BY semantics, the logical order a query is evaluated in, and three-valued logic: why `= NULL` never matches and how NULL breaks NOT IN.

picks.title: 06-02-basic-select-statement.mp4

picks.title: 06-07-null-values.mp4

picks.title: SQL Tutorial - Full Database Course for Beginners

picks.title: GROUPING SETS vs ROLLUP vs CUBE in SQL | Advanced SQL Tutorial with Examples

picks.title: GROUP BY and HAVING Clause in SQL

subtopics.name: Joins
subtopics.note: Inner, left, right, full and cross joins, self joins, how duplicates and NULLs multiply rows, and how databases execute joins (nested loop, hash, sort-merge).

picks.title: SQL JOINS Interview Question | What does different SQL Joins return?

picks.title: #12 - Join Algorithms: Hash, Sort-Merge, Nested Loop Joins (CMU Intro to Database Systems)
picks.why: How the database actually runs a join and what each algorithm costs. Answers "why is my join slow?"

picks.title: SQL WITH Clause | How to write SQL Queries using WITH Clause | SQL CTE (Common Table Expression)

subtopics.name: Window Functions
subtopics.note: OVER, PARTITION BY and ORDER BY; ROW_NUMBER vs RANK vs DENSE_RANK; LEAD/LAG; running totals and frame clauses. Very common in SQL rounds.

picks.title: SQL Window Function | How to write SQL Query using RANK, DENSE RANK, LEAD/LAG | SQL Queries Tutorial

picks.title: SQL Window Function | How to write SQL Query using Frame Clause, CUME_DIST | SQL Queries Tutorial

picks.title: SQL Window Functions | Clearly Explained | PARTITION BY, ORDER BY, ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK

picks.label: Triggers: Introduction (Stanford, Jennifer Widom)

picks.title: 11 02 constraints part1

subtopics.name: Indexing
subtopics.note: Why indexes speed up reads and slow down writes, B-tree vs B+tree, clustered vs non-clustered, composite indexes and the leftmost-prefix rule.

picks.title: B-tree vs B+ tree in Database Systems
picks.why: Why databases use B+trees: linked leaves for range scans and higher fan-out, plus what Postgres and MySQL do differently.

picks.title: #08 - Tree Indexes: B+Trees (CMU Intro to Database Systems)
picks.why: Insert, split, merge, clustered indexes and composite keys, as a database implements them.

picks.title: Understanding B-Trees: The Data Structure Behind Modern Databases

subtopics.name: Normalization
subtopics.note: Update, insert and delete anomalies; functional dependencies; 1NF to BCNF; lossless and dependency-preserving decomposition. Practise closure and candidate-key questions in the MCQs.

picks.title: Learn Database Normalization - 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, 4NF, 5NF
picks.why: Every normal form on one evolving example, each motivated by the anomaly it removes. The clearest normalization video there is.

picks.title: Learn Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF)
picks.why: Where 3NF and BCNF differ, which is a favourite follow-up question.

picks.title: 07-02-functional-dependencies.mp4
picks.why: Functional dependencies formally: closure, keys and the rules behind decomposition.
picks.label: Functional Dependencies (Stanford, Jennifer Widom)

subtopics.name: Transactions & Concurrency

picks.title: 12-02-transactions-properties.mp4
picks.why: ACID defined precisely, with what each property actually promises.
picks.label: Transaction Properties (Stanford, Jennifer Widom)

picks.title: 12-03-isolation-levels.mp4
picks.why: The isolation levels and exactly which anomalies each allows.
picks.label: Isolation Levels (Stanford, Jennifer Widom)

picks.title: #17 - Two-Phase Locking Concurrency Control (CMU Intro to Database Systems)

picks.title: #20 - MVCC: Multi-Version Concurrency Control (CMU Intro to Database Systems)

picks.title: "Transactions: myths, surprises and opportunities" by Martin Kleppmann

picks.title: ACID Properties in Databases With Examples
